monument_name: Devala Divyapura, śikhara temple 2 (from approx. 8th-10th century)
description_en: A shaiva śikhara temple from approx. 8th-10th century.The monument is part of a complex comprising five similar temples distributed accross a longitudinal platform oriented south-north. This platform, also known locally as Dewal Park, is located in the locality of Dewal Divyapur, 3 km west of Chipur and a dozen km north-west of Amargadhi, the district headquarters. The temples were seemingly all dedicated to Shaiva cult, as indicated by the presence ofjalaharīin the sanctums and oneśivaliṅga.Temple 2 is oriented to the east. It is composed of a single sanctum (Skt.garbhagṛha). There is no image in the sanctum. Instead, on the northern wall is an elevatedjalaharī-like support for a now-goneśivaliṅga. Thejalaharīgoes through the north wall and is visible from the outside. The sanctum was probably preceded by a short vestibule (Skt.antarāla). This element, as well as the door (doorjambs and lintel) and the pediment are missing. The roof is composed of horizontal bands and topped by a large stoneāmalakaring.These architectural features evoke temples built in Uttarakhand (India) around the 7th-8th century, and especially Temples 1 and 2 in Jageshwar (seeChanchani 2019, 81-83, fig. 3.7.). It may thus be suggested that this monument, as well as the four others found at the site, was built between the 8th and 10th century (Andolfatto 2022, 38;Sharma 2012, 284). This relative dating places the temples amongst the oldest known form of architecture in west Nepal.
identified_threats: Wall cracks, Other, Missing stones at plinths, Erosion
